clue.text: Top cut from this dipper served up for royalty

definitions.text: Top cut from this dipper served up for royalty

parts.words: Top cut from this dipper served up for royalty
parts.note: the dipper is a man who baptised others by immersion; his head was cut off and brought to Herod's court on a platter

explanation.surface: A bird's head is trimmed off and the dish presented to a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipper' looks like the bird, but here it means one who dips converts in water; 'top cut' is his beheading and 'served up for royalty' the platter brought for Herod and Salome.
explanation.definitionFit: The gospel story tells how the Baptist was beheaded and his head carried in on a dish for Herod's court.

clue.text: Stuff Roo with mashed heart of Kanga, feet of Pooh and Owl and half of Rabbit; add mush and liquor

annotationWithheld.why: Stuff Roo with mashed heart of Kanga, feet of Pooh and Owl and half of Rabbit; add mush and liquor: ROO, N, H, L and RAB leave J, E, Y, C, N unaccounted for, and no reading of 'mush' or 'Stuff' supplies them
annotationWithheld.clue: Stuff Roo with mashed heart of Kanga, feet of Pooh and Owl and half of Rabbit; add mush and liquor

clue.text: Man's attempt to secure love in bunk, allegedly

parts.note: 'man's' means belonging to him, his

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it inside, so the attempt wraps round love

parts.note: an attempt is a try
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man tries to get love while in his bunk bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford is supposed to have said that 'history is bunk', hence 'allegedly'; 'bunk' is nonsense, not a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford's famous dismissive remark called the study of the past nonsense, so the subject is bunk by his allegation.

clue.text: Clerk touring part of France picked up by salesperson

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the clerk's letters surround the French part

parts.note: a bank clerk at the counter is a teller

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted and read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the Var is a French department in Provence

explanation.surface: A clerk on a tour of a French region gets a lift from a sales rep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like collecting a passenger, but in a down clue it lifts the French department so that it reads upward before going into the clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is an old term for a sales representative who goes round visiting customers.

clue.text: The beginning of Lowry's Under the 17 down, without hesitation, is timeless

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places this piece below the others
without means outside, so the volcano's letters go round the hesitation

parts.note: the answer at 17 down names a fiery mountain, and Etna is one
er is the sound of a hesitation

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The opening of Malcolm Lowry's novel Under the Volcano, read straight through, has a timeless quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes Lowry's novel 'Under the Volcano', but 'Under' is the placing signal: L goes beneath ETERNA, the volcano Etna wrapped round the hesitation ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts for ever and so stands outside time, which is what timeless means.

clue.text: He hasn't been all there since the operation

definitions.text: He hasn't been all there since the operation

parts.words: He hasn't been all there since the operation
parts.note: 'not all there' usually means mentally lacking, but here a limb has literally been removed in surgery

explanation.surface: A man has been a little mentally vague since his surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not all there' suggests a confused mind; taken literally, part of the body is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has had a limb surgically removed is quite literally no longer complete in body.

clue.text: Compiler shouldering sea dogs' bones

indicators.note: in a down clue, the sailors carry the compiler on their shoulders, so they sit above

parts.note: a sea dog is an old sailor, and a tar is a sailor
the compiler, the setter, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter carries the bones of some old sailors on his shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsal bones form the ankle and back of the foot, a group of small bones.

clue.text: Take action about one inspectorate's voluntary exit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the lawsuit word goes round the rest

parts.note: to take legal action against someone is to sue
one is the Roman numeral I
the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch where inspectors work

explanation.surface: Legal action is brought over a police inspector's resignation.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one's own life is a departure from the world chosen by oneself, a euphemistic voluntary exit.

clue.text: Poet to go to the bathroom and take from the tap?

parts.note: john is American slang for the toilet
to take something from the tap is to drink water

explanation.surface: A poet heads to the bathroom and fills a glass from the tap.
explanation.walkthrough: John Drinkwater was an English poet and playwright of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinkwater was an English Georgian poet and dramatist, best known for his play about Abraham Lincoln.

clue.text: He's taken many years

parts.note: a host is a large number, many
an age is a long stretch of years

explanation.surface: He's been taking ages, many years in fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's taken' reads as an apology for delay, but it defines a person who has been seized.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held to force others' hand is a person who has been taken.

clue.text: There's little shelter from drink — one needs the poison

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, a drink
one is the Roman numeral I
CO is the chemical formula of carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas

explanation.surface: Little protection comes from booze if someone needs the poison too.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a small roofed porch at a building's entrance, giving a little cover.

clue.text: This fellow has no money, so changes banks

indicators.note: the banks of a river are right and left, so right is swapped for left

parts.note: someone with no money is broke

explanation.surface: A man who is broke moves his account from one bank to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks financial, but means the right and left banks of a river: R becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is informal British for a man, a fellow.

clue.text: There's sustenance when I turn into bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters are thrown into a mad new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds nourishment when they turn into bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is the food that nourishes, keeping a body sustained.

clue.text: Profligate has pound put back in the shade

annotationWithheld.why: Profligate has pound put back in the shade: ROUE round YALBL would need 'pound put back' to give YALBL, and no reading of profligate or pound found gives ROYAL BLUE
annotationWithheld.clue: Profligate has pound put back in the shade

clue.text: Feminist offers snarl, having got poor grades

indicators.note: having got means holding, so the snarl contains the grades

parts.note: grr is the sound of a snarl
E is a low mark, so two of them are poor grades

explanation.surface: A feminist snarls at receiving bad marks.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist author of The Female Eunuch.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer wrote The Female Eunuch and is a leading second-wave feminist writer.

clue.text: Liberator needs a wife: enter the young Lady Diana

indicators.note: enter means go inside, so the wife goes into the girl

parts.note: a gal is a young woman, a girl
rib is a jocular word for a wife, after Eve made from Adam's rib
Di is the short form of Diana

explanation.surface: A liberator needs a wife, so in comes the young Lady Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Diana' looks like one famous name, but 'the young Lady' and 'Diana' are separate pieces; calling a wife a rib recalls Eve, made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the fight to free and unify Italy, so he is remembered as its liberator.

clue.text: The Queen's round number

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the cipher goes round the other word

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Queen orders a round of drinks, a certain number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' means something that numbs: ether was an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was used as a general anaesthetic, so it is a substance that makes people numb.

clue.text: House share with a one-eyed philosopher?

parts.note: a ratio is a proportion, a share

explanation.surface: Sharing a house with a philosopher who has lost an eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Nelson lost an eye; Hamlet's friend Horatio is told of things not dreamt of in his philosophy: the question mark marks the combination.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to one-eyed Admiral Nelson and to Hamlet's scholarly friend, combined playfully here.

clue.text: Parish councillor offering terms with navy rum

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A parish councillor offers some sailors' terms along with navy rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink after 'navy', but is the British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestryman is a member of a parish vestry, the body that runs a church's affairs.

clue.text: When cut up, Love has power — Love has destructive power

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom upward
cut means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
can means is able to, has the power
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Love, when hurt, is powerful, even destructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims LOVE to LOV and 'up' turns it to VOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano erupts with enormous destructive force, a natural power that devastates the land.

clue.text: Hone the right to be informed?

indicators.note: read with the next word as 'to be in formed', putting the right letter inside

parts.note: split as in plus formed, and shapen is an old word for formed
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Honing one's right to be kept in the know.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'informed' as 'in formed': R is put in SHAPEN, an old word for shaped or formed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hone a blade is to put a keen edge on it.

clue.text: Doctor gets big reduction, they say, on Russian cocktail

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a lot off is a big reduction in price

explanation.surface: A doctor's big discount on a Russian drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Vyacheslav Molotov was a Soviet foreign minister whose name was given to a petrol bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian statesman Molotov gave his name to the improvised petrol bomb called a Molotov cocktail.

clue.text: Canned beer (stored in the usual place) runs out, we think

indicators.note: stored in means kept inside, so the shuffled beer goes inside
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, so it goes out of the word

parts.note: beer is usually stored in a cellar

indicators.note: canned is slang for drunk, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Canned beer, normally kept in the cellar, has run out, we suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like tinned, but is slang for drunk; EREB from BEER goes into CELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is part of the brain, the organ with which we think; the plural names those parts.

clue.text: Begin a different way of life?

indicators.note: these letters set out a different way make another word

explanation.surface: Start a new way of life?
explanation.definitionFit: Being means existence, the state of being alive.

clue.text: Smack with Ecstasy kept under the hatches

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the blow holds the drug

parts.note: a smack is a blow
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Heroin and ecstasy hidden under the ship's hatches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like slang for heroin, matching 'Ecstasy', but means a hit; on a ship, below is beneath the hatches.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, being below deck means being under the hatches.

clue.text: Wine box upset, losing top

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the letters are reversed
losing top means the first letter goes

parts.note: a canister is a box or container

explanation.surface: A wine box is knocked over and loses its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: ANISTER, from 'losing top', is turned round by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: White rum, say, means something to Don

parts.note: white is pale
a tot is a small measure of a spirit such as rum

explanation.surface: White rum means something to a university don.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, but is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose overcoat, a garment that one puts on.

clue.text: Drinker of rum and winter warmers will get liver damage

parts.note: long johns are long underpants worn for warmth in winter

indicators.note: damage means harm, so the letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone wearing winter underwear will damage their liver.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the rum-drinking pirate of Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate of Stevenson's Treasure Island is a great drinker of rum, like his crew.
